newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan pays money to former sex slaves.
newsitem.headline: Japan pays money to former sex slaves.

text.p: Seven South Korean women who were used as sex-slaves by the Japanese army during World War Two, have each been paid 5 million yen ($43,000), the Japanese fund set up to compensate the "comfort women" said on Sunday.
"Funds were paid from the Asian Women's Fund to seven (South Korean) women on Saturday," a spokesman for the fund said.
But the action provoked a bitter reaction from the South Korean government, which along with other Asian nations, has sharply criticised Japan's handling of the issue.
Most of the women forced into sexual service for the Japanese military have refused to accept any of the money, which comes from a private fund and not directly from the Japanese government.
"The South Korean government regrets the Japanese action to deliver the money to the comfort women without acknowledging the seriousness of the issue," it said in a statement.
The issue has been an emotional one among Asian countries, part of a larger debate over whether Japan has properly atoned for its military actions a half century ago.

It also has political overtones in Japan. The ruling Liberal Democratic Party has a strong element that believes Japan has gone too far in apologising. Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto sparked criticism in the summer when he visited a shrine honouring Japan's war dead.
The women were given 2 million yen ($17,000) in compensation and a further 3 million yen ($26,000) for medical treatment.
Each also received a letter of apology from Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, the fund said.

A South Korean women's group, the Korean Council for Women Drafted for Military Sexual Slavery by Japan, strongly opposes compensation by the nominally private fund. It wants the Japanese government to compensate the victims directly.
Japan has refused to open negotiations for state compensation, saying all war reparations had been closed with peace treaties signed in the 1950s and 1960s.

The Asian Women's Fund, initiated by the Japanese government, was established in July 1995 to compensate what historians estimate was up to 200,000 women from Korea and other Japanese-occupied territories in Asia who were forced into sexual slavery for Japanese soldiers before and during the war.
The former sex slaves are euphemistically called "comfort women" in Japan.

On August 13 last year, Hashimoto admitted Japan's moral responsibility for dishonouring Asian women by forcing them into sexual slavery in a letter of apology to former wartime sex slaves in the Philippines.

Eight of at least 169 Filipino women registered by the fund as having been forced into sexual servitude at wartime front-line brothels have accepted the money, together with a letter of apology from Hashimoto.
